title: Transcriptome-based classification in mice with ASD-risk mutations.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found GEO SuperSeries GSE293709 (1,565 bulk samples) by searching GEO, since PubMed had no links. Opened its batch sheet: 1,008 discovery cortex samples at P25 (postnatal day 25) across 17 sub-series and 8 batches, plus 175 validation, 269 hippocampus and 113 P40 samples. Downloaded all 20 cortex DESeq-normalized matrices (170 MB). Each parses first try, with 18,088 Ensembl genes (51,456 in the validation sets), 0 NA, 0 duplicate genes, and genotype/drug/sex encoded in column names; the matrices hold 1,010 discovery columns. Quick leave-one-line-out logistic regression: sex AUC (area under the ROC curve) 1.0, lithium 0.99 median, fluoxetine 0.81 median, mutant vs wild-type 0.53, shuffled labels 0.50. Also listed snRNA-seq (single-nucleus RNA sequencing) series GSE330728: 13.6 GB of MTX files and a 212-row mouse-to-pool table.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The two-group (group 1 / group 2) assignments, the human 40-vs-17 cortex comparison, and the paper's classifier method and accuracy all come from the abstract and press coverage. There is no open full text, so I did not see the data availability statement or the code.

a1_downloadable.note: All bulk sub-series matrices download from GEO FTP without login. Checked in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Genotype (H/W), drug (v/f/L) and sex (M/F) are encoded in every sample column name and in the batch sheet. The paper's group 1/group 2 label is NOT a column and would have to be reconstructed from expression.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full normalized expression matrices are present: 18,088 genes × samples per line. Checked.

a4_units_stated.note: Files are labelled 'processed_data_DESeq': DESeq2 size-factor-normalized counts, one normalization per sub-series. Units are implied by the file name rather than documented.

a5_enough_rows.note: 1,008 discovery samples in the batch sheet (1,010 columns in the matrices), plus 175 validation samples. But the independent unit is the mouse line (17 discovery, 3 validation), or about 34 line×sex groups.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~170 MB compressed; ~1,200 × 18,088 float matrix, about 0.2 GB in RAM
a6_fits_laptop.note: Whole probe ran in seconds on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The batch sheet's 1,008 matches the abstract. The matrices have 1,010 columns (2 extra, e.g. GSE293627 has 59 columns vs 57 in the sheet), which is trivially reconcilable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Genotype, drug and sex are experimental-design facts, not model outputs. The paper's group labels are clusters computed from this same expression data, so predicting them would be circular and they must not be used as a target.

B1.why: 20 per-line matrices with an identical 18,088-gene index plus one batch sheet; joins cleanly (checked).

B2.why: All tab-separated gz files parsed first try: 0 NA, 0 duplicate genes, all numeric.

B3.why: DESeq normalization is done per line, so the line is confounded with normalization and batch; cross-line rescaling is needed.

B4.why: No censored values; continuous normalized counts and categorical design labels.

B5.why: No duplicate genes or samples found; 2-column surplus versus the batch sheet is minor.

B6.why: Column-name code (H/W, v/f/L, M/F) is decodable via the batch sheet, but there is no README.

C1.why: 'Does a drug or mutation signature learned on 17 lines transfer to new lines/region/age?' is informative either way.

C2.why: Only the paper's own classifier exists; code availability unseen. No other ML on this dataset found.

C3.why: Weak unique-application angle: drug-exposure transfer across genotypes; the main classification is the paper's own result.

C4.why: Mouse-line RNA-seq is costly, but the classification step itself is cheap clustering.

C5.why: Obvious dummies verified: shuffled AUC 0.50; mutant-vs-WT 0.53; sex 1.0; lithium 0.99.

D1.why: No bulk-mouse-brain backbone; Geneformer/scGPT are single-cell, mostly human; fit is poor.

D2.why: Could embed the snRNA-seq with scGPT, but 13.6 GB needs subsetting; bulk does not benefit.

D3.why: GEO data is open; backbone licences vary; nothing restrictive found.

E1.why: Leave-one-line-out split is natural; separate validation lines, hippocampus and P40 series exist (checked).

E2.why: 17 discovery lines plus 3 validation lines, each with about 60 mice.

E3.why: Majority class and shuffled-label baselines computed: AUC 0.50.

E4.why: About 5 replicate mice per genotype×drug×sex cell give a within-group noise floor.

E5.why: Sex classification across held-out lines gives AUC 1.0 (verified); the mutated gene's own dosage is a second control.

E6.why: Within-line label shuffle ran; collapsed to 0.50.

E7.why: Validation lines (Shank2, Chd8-S62X, Ank2), hippocampus and P40 series are separate batches (checked).

E8.why: The paper's classifier accuracy and code were not seen; there is no full text.

G1.why: Ensembl mouse gene IDs (ENSMUSG) in every matrix.

G2.why: Plausible partners: human ASD cortex RNA-seq (PsychENCODE), SFARI gene list; not verified joinable.

G3.why: Mouse-to-human ortholog mapping is one-to-many in places.

G4.why: Transferring the mouse two-state signature to human cortex is the paper's own extension.

H1.why: Wild-type littermates, vehicle controls and both sexes in every line (checked).

H2.why: One lab, one strain (C57BL/6J), one age per series, heterozygous mutants only.

H3.why: Claim is precise: transfer across these 20 lines in one lab's P25 prefrontal cortex.

H4.why: Single-lab design is obvious; per-line normalization confound is not stated in the abstract.

I1.why: ASD mouse-model and SFARI community; Eunjoon Kim's lab (KAIST).

I2.why: Might guide which drug to test per line; marginal.

I3.why: AUC for drug/genotype detection only roughly matches a 'responder' decision.

I4.why: Sex and lithium are trivially separable; genotype transfer fails linearly; ML adds little beyond clustering.

J1.why: Grouped CV and transfer on clean bulk data; little transfer learning.

J2.why: Needs neurogenetics intuition to judge synaptic/chromatin signatures.

J3.why: A clean 1,200-sample combined matrix plus transfer benchmark is shareable at each step.

J4.why: About 1–2 weeks plausible; not formally set.

existing_models.name: Roh et al. 2026 transcriptome-based two-group classifier (this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to classify independent mouse lines; exact metric and split not seen (no full text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not seen. Press coverage says group membership flips by sex in 7 of 17 lines and is less distinct in human cortex.

backbone.name: none suitable for bulk; scGPT (single-cell foundation model) only for the snRNA-seq subset
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop for bulk; snRNA-seq would need subsetting

integration.partner_dataset: PsychENCODE / human ASD postmortem cortex RNA-seq
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do drug-response signatures learned across 17 mouse mutation lines predict which human ASD cortex subgroup a sample resembles?

controls.positive_control: Sex prediction across held-out lines (verified AUC 1.0); lithium exposure (verified median AUC 0.99).
controls.external_validation: Validation lines GSE294123/5/7 (Shank2, Chd8-S62X, Ank2), hippocampus GSE319614, P40 cortex GSE319615-20.

honest_claim_h3: Within one lab's P25 prefrontal cortex from heterozygous C57BL/6J mice, a drug- or mutation-exposure classifier trained on 17 lines does (or does not) transfer to 3 new lines, the hippocampus and P40.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use brain gene-expression profiles from mutant mice to predict drug exposure and mutation status in mouse lines the model never saw.
plain_idea.train_on: Prefrontal-cortex expression of 18,088 genes for each of 1,008 mice from 17 autism-risk mutant lines and their wild-type littermates (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a mouse carries the mutation and which drug (vehicle, fluoxetine or lithium) it received; truth comes from the breeding genotype and the treatment the experimenters gave.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tells autism mouse-model labs whether a shared mutation or drug signature exists across genes; a quick check found generic mutation detection at chance (AUC 0.53), which supports the paper's two-opposing-states finding.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use the same 1,008 + 175 samples the paper's classifier used.

confidence_score.why: About 5 replicate mice per condition allow per-line uncertainty estimates; unknown whether the paper reports them.

models_beatable.why: The paper's 2026 classifier is unseen; it is likely clustering-based, but it is the authors' own framing on their own data.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new joinable data measures the same quantity the same way; other labs' mouse-model RNA-seq differs in age, region and batch.

label_elsewhere.sources: Other GEO mouse ASD-model brain RNA-seq series, e.g. GSE134526 (Tbr1-K228E whole brain, 15 samples), seen in a GEO search; also GSE271853 (human stem-cell ASD models, 476 samples).
label_elsewhere.join_key: Ensembl mouse gene ID; mutated gene symbol
label_elsewhere.why: Independent mutant-vs-wild-type brain profiles from other labs could test whether signatures survive lab and batch changes, but ages and regions differ.

ambitious.why: Publishes biology-first genomics; would need a drug-response signature that transfers to new lines and to human ASD cortex subgroups.

realistic.why: Publishes reanalyses of ASD model data; a leave-one-line-out transfer benchmark of mutation/drug signatures fits.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics
fallback.why: A clean combined matrix and a negative 'no shared mutation signature' benchmark result is publishable as a resource note.

pitch.headline: 1,008 prefrontal transcriptomes from 17 autism-mutant mouse lines, sex-balanced, each with vehicle/fluoxetine/lithium arms, all open on GEO as 170 MB of clean tables.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: One lab, one protocol, 17 lines × 2 genotypes × 3 drugs × 2 sexes at about 5 mice per cell, plus separate validation lines, hippocampus and P40 series (1,565 samples total; verified).
pitch.the_win: A drug-exposure classifier trained on 17 lines that keeps fluoxetine AUC above 0.81 (current quick median) on the 3 held-out validation lines and the hippocampus.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Already shown in a quick check: mutation status does not transfer across lines (AUC 0.53), which quantifies that no shared autism-mutation signature exists linearly.
pitch.who_wants_it: Autism mouse-model labs (e.g. Eunjoon Kim's group, SFARI-funded labs) choosing which drug to test on which mutant line.

ml_idea: Combine the 20 per-line DESeq matrices; run leave-one-line-out classification of genotype and drug exposure, then test transfer to the validation lines, the hippocampus and the P40 series. Avoid the paper's group labels as targets (they are circular).

effort.compute_note: Timed: download plus a full leave-one-line-out logistic regression on 1,185 samples × 2,000 genes took seconds on the laptop CPU.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Rescale the per-line normalization (e.g. within-line wild-type centering) and see whether fluoxetine transfer stays above 0.75 AUC on the 3 validation lines; if not, there is no transferable signal.

verdict_reason: Data is open, clean and laptop-sized (verified), but the prediction tasks are either trivial (sex, lithium at AUC ~1.0), circular (the paper's expression-derived groups) or at chance (mutation status, 0.53). There is no fitting pretrained backbone, and the effective sample is 17–20 lines.
